Breaking: Raptors' RJ Barrett out with strained right hamstring, Collin Murray-Boyles placed in concussion protocol

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (314 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toronto Raptors forward RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the team confirmed Thursday.
  • Additionally, forward Collin Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol as a precautionary measure.
  • According to recent reports, barrett missed Wednesday's 103-99 loss to the Washington Wizards with hamstring tightness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toronto Raptors forward RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the team confirmed Thursday.

Additionally, forward Collin Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol as a precautionary measure.

According to recent reports, barrett missed Wednesday's 103-99 loss to the Washington Wizards with hamstring tightness. That was the second of back-to-back games for the Raptors, who also lost to the Fresh York Knicks on Tuesday. Barrett played 39 minutes in that game, scoring 22 points with 5 rebounds and 5 assists.

According to recent reports, however, hamstring discomfort has been an issue for Barrett in recent weeks. He has been using a stationary bike on the sideline when not on the court, in addition to during timeouts and stoppages in play, according to The Athletic's Esfandiar Baraheni.

Sources indicate that murray-Boyles left Wednesday's contest during the first half after playing four minutes. The Raptors announced that he would not return due to illness, which has apparently been going around the team locker room. When he sustained a possible concussion is not certain.

Industry observers note that barrett, 26, is Toronto's second-leading scorer this season, averaging 20.9 points with 6.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game. He's shooting a career-low 28% on 74 3-point attempts. Prior to sitting out Wednesday's contest, Barrett had appeared in all 14 of the Raptors' games.

Recent findings suggest that in his second season, Murray-Boyles is averaging 9.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists, in addition to 1 steal and 1.1 blocks in 14 games (eight starts). He was the Raptors' 2025 first-round pick (No. 9 overall) out of South Carolina.

Toronto (5-10) has lost its past six games and eight of its past 10. The Raptors currently rank ninth in the Eastern Conference and 16th in the NBA. They visit the Detroit Pistons (10-4) on Friday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the epicenters of above-average dividend yields and, in many cases, alluring dividend growth is the energy sector, specifically pipeline stocks.
  • MPLX (MPLX -1.55%) is certainly part of that conversation.
  • It's one of the most impressive dividend growth stories among large-cap midstream equities, and that's saying something because that asset class is ripe with high yields and stout payout-growth trajectories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Todd Shriber – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than MPLX ›.

One of the epicenters of above-average dividend yields and, in many cases, alluring dividend growth is the energy sector, specifically pipeline stocks.

MPLX (MPLX -1.55%) is certainly part of that conversation. This master limited partnership (MLP) stores and transports natural gas and oil in the Marcellus Basin in eastern North America and the Permian Basin in Texas, among other locations.

It's one of the most impressive dividend growth stories among large-cap midstream equities, and that's saying something because that asset class is ripe with high yields and stout payout-growth trajectories.

MPLX made good on a promise to lift its distribution by 12.5% and the payout growth could continue. Image source: Getty Images.

Sources indicate that in conjunction with its third-quarter earnings report released on Nov. 3, the company declared its third consecutive 12.5% annual dividend increase, putting it in a strong position to honor its previously announced pledge to grow its distribution by 12.5% annually through at least 2027.

With the latest dividend increase announcement, MPLX yields an eye-catching 8.5%, and its yearly payout in dollar terms vaults to $4.84 per share. So that means investors who owned $10,000 (and all shareholders, for that matter) of this midstream stock before this month are getting raises.

In a recent development, based on the Nov. 13 closing price of $57.25, $10,000 buys 174.6 shares. Let's simplify the math and call that 175 shares. With the fresh payout of $4.84 a share, 175 shares generate $847 in yearly income. That's pretty good.

It's even better for investors who don't need that income right now. They can -- and probably should -- consider the merits of dividend reinvestment, particularly if the pipeline operator makes good on its pledge to grow its payout by 12.5% again next year.

Figure it this way: With a $10,000 stake, even if the stock were to trade flat for a year, the $847 in dividends investors will receive over the next 12 months would buy another 14.7 shares based on the Nov. 13 closing prices.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

According to recent reports, it might not sound like much, but that's nearly another $72 added to an investor's compounding mix with MPLX. Plus, based on the company's $1.5 billion in third-quarter distributable cash flow, it's generating enough cash flow to cover its shareholder rewards obligations.

    3 Social Security Spousal Benefit Rules Too Many Couples Don't Know About

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (484 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, being married in retirement has its perks.
    • Industry observers note that being married could also be advantageous from a Social Security perspective.
    • Recent findings suggest that but if you're expecting to file for spousal benefits, it's vital to understand how they work.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:02AM EST.

    In a recent development, being married in retirement has its perks. You have someone to split the housework with, spend time with, and make financial decisions with.

    Industry observers note that being married could also be advantageous from a Social Security perspective. Even if one of you doesn't have enough of a work history to qualify for Social Security on your own, you may be eligible for one regular retirement benefit and one spousal benefit at the same time.

    Recent findings suggest that but if you're expecting to file for spousal benefits, it's vital to understand how they work. Here are three rules couples tend to overlook.

    Recent findings suggest that when you're filing for Social Security based on your own earnings record, the earliest age to take benefits is 62. That's also the earliest age to file for spousal benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that but if you claim spousal benefits at 62, you'll reduce them in the process. Plus, that may not even be an option if your spouse hasn't filed for their benefits yet.

    Recent findings suggest that when you're signing up for Social Security based on your own earnings record, there's a huge incentive to wait past full retirement age. Each year you sit tight until you turn 70 gives your benefits a permanent 8% boost.

    According to recent reports, that boost does not apply to spousal Social Security benefits, though. The most a spousal benefit is worth is 50% of your spouse's full retirement age benefit. And you'll get that maximum spousal benefit at your full retirement age. Filing later won't make your monthly checks any larger.

    Sources indicate that it may be that you're eligible for Social Security based on your own wage history, and that you're entitled to spousal benefits as well. You can collect the larger of those two benefits. But you can't receive both at the same time.

    According to recent reports, social Security will only pay you one benefit at once. If you're entitled to $1,000 a month based on your own earnings history but $1,050 a month in spousal benefits, you'll receive the latter.

    According to recent reports, social Security is a complicated program in its own right. What makes things even trickier is that spousal benefits have their own set of rules. It's key to familiarize yourself with how spousal benefits work if you expect them to play a role in your household's retirement income.

    By Will Healy – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +17.07%) stock had a surprisingly lackluster first day of trading. While its opening price of $111.50 per share was well above its $83 per share IPO price, and it briefly headed toward almost $115, the stock began to slide within minutes. By the close of trading, it was at $97.17 per share — 13% below the opening price. Given that performance, investors may want to consider buying the stock, albeit with a more cautious approach.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    Admittedly, many stocks gain ground quickly at their debut. This is especially true of well-known businesses like Anthropic, whose Claude AI Assistant has become a top choice for many customers.

    Moreover, at a market cap of $1.76 trillion as of the time of this writing, Anthropic is now trading at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of around 50.

    Sources indicate that although that amounts to a significant premium, investors might be willing to pay it given the company’s  1,127% revenue growth in the third quarter. Assuming Anthropic’s rapid growth continues for a few more quarters, the stock could actually be a bargain.

    However, investors need to remember that the purpose of IPOs is to raise money, meaning they tend to occur well into bull markets. This often sets such stocks up for steep declines when the broader sentiment turns bearish, which is why these stocks can end up trading below their IPO prices for extended periods.

    Industry observers note that additionally, the sell-off that took place after its brief early surge suggests that investors have less appetite for this SaaS stock than they did for Space Exploration Technologies(SPCX -3.53%). SpaceX debuted in June and surged by as much as 49% above its IPO price in its first few trading days before pulling back to well below that level over the following month. As of the close on Thursday, SpaceX was trading at around $137 — just above its IPO price, and well below its first trading price.

    It has been revealed that the problem with Anthropic stock is that its near-term path is uncertain. As of the time of this writing, it is unclear whether Anthropic will dive below its IPO price or gear up for a recovery.

    Indeed, its rapid revenue growth and relatively low valuation relative to its sales growth outlook suggest that investors should consider buying some shares. Yet considering its volatility, as well as the commonly poor performance of IPO stocks, investors who want to add Anthropic shares to their portfolios should probably do so slowly and build their positions incrementally.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • In a recent development, cathie Wood's investment firm, Ark Invest, has long been a fan of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -3.53%).
    • After the SpaceX IPO, Ark Invest disclosed a 4.48 million-share stake.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    In a recent development, cathie Wood's investment firm, Ark Invest, has long been a fan of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -3.53%). Its funds owned private SpaceX shares before the space stock even went public.

    After the SpaceX IPO, Ark Invest disclosed a 4.48 million-share stake. Over the next 90 days, the firm purchased an additional 2.28 million shares, upping its stake by roughly 50%.

    Last week, Ark Invest added another $96 million in SpaceX stock across three of its ETFs, even as it sold $122 million in Broadcom (AVGO -2.09%), another popular AI stock.

    In a recent development, why is Wood continuing to bet on SpaceX even as shares hover near its original IPO price? There's one obvious reason to remain bullish.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    It has been revealed that in early November, Cathie Wood was interviewed by CNBC. In this interview, she revealed her firm's recent purchases of SpaceX stock, noting that they were part of a larger portfolio repositioning following the AI stock sell-off. Ark Invest, she explained, wanted to concentrate its bets on its highest-conviction investments.

    Why exactly is SpaceX a high-conviction name for Wood after the pullback?

    "Our SpaceX position has gone up," Wood told CNBC, immediately adding that "The controversy around data centers on Earth is giving data centers in space a bigger opportunity.".

    It's no surprise that AI is critical to SpaceX's long-term growth. AI comprises $26.5 trillion of the company's claimed $28.5 trillion total addressable market. Successfully deploying orbital data centers (ODCs) is critical to realizing much of that growth potential.

    More than $7 trillion is projected to be spent on data center infrastructure over the next few years alone, giving SpaceX plenty of market to penetrate. Boston Consulting Group estimates that SpaceX could capture 10%–15% of the global AI data center market by 2040, generating between $240 billion and $320 billion in annual revenue.

    "Our analysis indicates that space-based data centers could become technically feasible at scale within the next five to ten years," the firm concludes. "It won't be a trivial layer, either.".

    Morningstar estimates, meanwhile, call for $225 billion in annual revenue for SpaceX's orbital computing business by 2035, with the company capturing 20% of the global AI data center market by 2040 in its bull scenario.

    Wood's firm, Ark Invest, hasn't been shy about its bullishness on ODCs.

    "As the build-out expands, data center economics on the ground are likely to get worse as developers cope with local opposition and have to find exponentially increasing amounts of power. Meanwhile, SpaceX should become increasingly expert at manufacturing its satellites and packing more satellites into each launch," research from the firm concludes, adding that ODC growth should be "much larger than consensus models have incorporated.".

    The ODC opportunity is clear. Execution risk, however, is high. Morningstar believes there's only a 7% chance that ODCs scale as Elon Musk projects.

    Sources indicate that I'm in a similar boat -- a reality that has kept me on the sidelines this year. But if you're bullish on the long-term promise of ODCs, it's not hard to understand why Wood keeps adding to her SpaceX position.

    Oracle Stock Just Closed at Its Lowest Price Since April 2024. Is It a Buy Now?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Oracle (ORCL -2.92%) stock finished Wednesday, Nov.
    • According to recent reports, that price is even under what Oracle's latest shareholders paid.
    • It has been revealed that still, the business keeps speeding up.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:47AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Oracle ›.

    Oracle (ORCL -2.92%) stock finished Wednesday, Nov. 18, at $113.89, its lowest close since April 30, 2024. Shares are now around 65% below their record close of $328.33 in September 2025, and they're off about 42% so far in 2026.

    According to recent reports, that price is even under what Oracle's latest shareholders paid. On Nov. 2, the cloud giant priced 86.2 million new shares at $116 each. After underwriting fees, Oracle kept around $114.59 a share.

    It has been revealed that still, the business keeps speeding up. Oracle expects revenue to grow 30% to 34% year over year in its fiscal second quarter, which ends later this month.

    But I think the profit side of that forecast matters more for the stock, and it doesn't look as strong.

    In a recent development, showing how fast its cloud infrastructure business is ramping, Oracle's revenue climbed 30% year over year to $19.3 billion in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 (the three months ended Aug. 31, 2026). That was an acceleration from the 21% and 22% growth in the two quarters before it -- and from just 14% in the quarter before that. Cloud infrastructure revenue alone surged 121% to $7.4 billion.

    It has been revealed that also, Oracle booked over $30 billion in new artificial intelligence (AI) cloud contracts during fiscal Q1. That raised its remaining performance obligations (contracted revenue it hasn't recognized yet) to $664 billion.

    The fiscal Q2 guidance calls for that rate to hold or even pick up.

    Earnings, however, aren't expected to keep up.

    According to recent reports, over the past three reported quarters, Oracle's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share climbed about as fast as revenue did. It rose 21% in fiscal Q3, 20% in fiscal Q4 (excluding one-time investment gains), and 30% in fiscal Q1.

    The fiscal Q2 forecast breaks that pattern. Management sees earnings per share between $1.85 and $1.93 on an adjusted basis. When a one-time gain from selling Oracle's stake in chipmaker Ampere is taken out of the year-ago quarter, that's growth of 21% to 25%, or around 9 percentage points behind the revenue guide.

    It has been revealed that the gap probably comes from costs that show up before the revenue does. Oracle's depreciation more than doubled to $3.2 billion in fiscal Q1 as new data centers came online. Interest expense rose 55% as its borrowing grew. And the $20 billion of stock Oracle sold under an at-the-market program that quarter spreads its earnings across more shares.

    Sure, Oracle's long-term plan already allows for some of this. At its Oct. 28 investor day, management targeted a non-GAAP operating margin of 40% or higher in fiscal 2030, a little under the 42% it hit in fiscal Q1. But it still calls for at least $21 a share in adjusted earnings that year. Getting there from the $8.10 Oracle sees this fiscal year would take earnings growth of around 37% a year.

    In a recent development, demand has to hold up, too. Bloomberg reported on Nov. 6 that Microsoft is phasing out a 2023 deal to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle, reportedly because the servers had older graphics chips. Oracle said demand for its AI infrastructure is still strong, older chips included.

    Industry observers note that true, one deal of undisclosed size is small next to a $664 billion backlog. But it shows that customers might quit paying for older hardware when better chips arrive.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    Recent findings suggest that at roughly $114, Oracle shares trade at about 14 times this fiscal year's expected earnings. That uses the $8.10 in adjusted earnings per share management is guiding for in the year ending May 31, 2027. For comparison, the S&P 500 is priced at about 18 times the earnings its companies are expected to make in the next 12 months. That's a discount to the average substantial organization, though Oracle's $8.10 target is about 19% above fiscal 2026's adjusted earnings per share, excluding one-time gains.

    Sources indicate that when I covered Oracle's latest funding cap in late October, the stock was around $145, or about 18 times the same expected earnings. I called that a fair price. Oracle reaffirmed its $8.10 target at its investor day, and the shares have since dropped about 21%.

    It has been revealed that does that make Oracle stock worth buying now? I think it's worth a look, even with the heaviest spending still ahead. Management expects capital expenditures to peak this fiscal year and next, and it doesn't see positive free cash flow until the second half of fiscal 2028.

    Sources indicate that fiscal Q2 still needs to show earnings growth in the 21%-to-25% range, and a miss might drive shares down. But at this price, I think the stock already allows profits to trail sales for a while.

    #3640. Industry News: Moderna vs. BioNTech: Why Only 1 Is a Buy Heading Into 2027

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (776 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Moderna vs. BioNTech: Why Only 1 Is a Buy Heading Into 2027

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the coronavirus pandemic turned two little-known mRNA companies into household names.
    • This year, their paths have diverged.
    • So, heading into 2027, which of these mRNA pioneers is the better buy?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adria Cimino – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Moderna ›.

    According to recent reports, the coronavirus pandemic turned two little-known mRNA companies into household names. Moderna (MRNA +1.29%) and BioNTech (BNTX -2.26%) brought their vaccines to market, collected billions of dollars in revenue, and then watched demand fade in recent years. Both stocks fell significantly from their highs, and both companies have spent the past few years trying to prove they're more than coronavirus vaccine makers.

    This year, their paths have diverged. Moderna's stock has soared as investors rushed to bet on the company's promising personalized cancer vaccine program. BioNTech, meanwhile, saw its stock price slip and prepared to say goodbye to its founders.

    So, heading into 2027, which of these mRNA pioneers is the better buy?

    Recent findings suggest that first, a quick recap. Both companies have faced the same problem: the coronavirus vaccine was a windfall that couldn't last. Moderna's product sales peaked at more than $18 billion in 2022, and BioNTech's reached a high of about the same level in 2021. Each responded by cutting costs and shifting toward oncology. BioNTech has more than 25 phase 2 and phase 3 clinical trials ongoing in that treatment area. Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine candidate, intismeran autogene, is involved in four phase 3 trials and several earlier-stage trials.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    In a recent development, bioNTech has real strengths. It has more than $17 billion in cash and investments, and its lead candidate, pumitamig, is a bispecific antibody it's developing with Bristol Myers Squibb. The firm is evaluating pumitamig in seven global pivotal studies across several cancer types. Meanwhile, BioNTech recently had mixed results in a phase 3 trial of an antibody-drug conjugate with DualityBio. Though the candidate met its primary endpoint, its impact may be "limited," the companies mentioned.

    The coronavirus vaccine remains BioNTech's only commercialized product for the moment as we wait for the pipeline to potentially produce others. And the company will see its CEO, Uğur Şahin, and chief medical officer, Özlem Türeci, leave at year-end. A latest CEO takes over by Feb. 1. That's a lot of change during a critical stretch.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    Moderna, by contrast, has several commercialized products. Third-quarter revenue rose 29% to $1.3 billion, and net income was $162 million, a big swing from a loss a year earlier. Management raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to a range of 15% to 25%, up from an earlier forecast of up to 10%. The biotech company now has five approved products, including a flu vaccine approved in the U.S. this year. A limited launch has already delivered more than 110,000 vaccinations, and Moderna is preparing a broader rollout for the 2027-2028 respiratory season.

    The bigger prize is oncology, and in a phase 3 melanoma trial, intismeran plus Merck's Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. Intismeran is also in studies for lung, bladder, and kidney cancers, so melanoma could be just the first of several revenue streams.

    Next year offers several potential catalysts. Moderna and Merck mentioned they'd be in contact with regulators about filing for intismeran approval, so investors should watch for submission news. Moderna will also provide formal 2027 financial guidance with its fourth-quarter report, and it's still awaiting FDA guidance on refiling its flu and COVID combination vaccine. Finally, in Europe, Moderna expects an opportunity to gain share as a competitor's COVID-19 vaccine contract expires.

    Moderna isn't risk-free. The tech giant still must gain regulatory approval for intismeran and prove the candidate's strength in several other clinical trials, and the stock's huge run raises expectations. Investors may see volatility around 2027 guidance.

    Sources indicate that bioNTech has the cash and a promising pipeline, and it may reward patient investors down the road. But its biggest opportunities are further out, and it's navigating a leadership overhaul along the way. Moderna offers a rarer combination: growing sales today, a cancer therapy that could reach the market soon, and a broadening vaccine lineup. That's why Moderna is my pick between the two, to buy and hold for the long term.

    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • Since taking the helm as chief executive officer of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.52%) (BRKB -0.45%) in January, Greg Abel has made several major acquisitions and investments.
    • But among the changes to the Warren Buffett investments made by his predecessor, Abel's biggest deal thus far has been further investment in Google parent Alphabet (GOOG -2.93%) (GOOGL -3.46%), increasing the company’s position by $10 billion last June.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Since taking the helm as chief executive officer of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.52%) (BRKB -0.45%) in January, Greg Abel has made several major acquisitions and investments. These include the purchase of homebuilder Taylor Morrison, the sale of long-held positions in stocks such as Mastercard and Visa, and a ramp-up in the repurchase of Berkshire Hathaway shares.

    But among the changes to the Warren Buffett investments made by his predecessor, Abel's biggest deal thus far has been further investment in Google parent Alphabet (GOOG -2.93%) (GOOGL -3.46%), increasing the company’s position by $10 billion last June. With this further investment, Abel seems to be making Alphabet a core holding, perhaps as a long-term bet on the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.

    Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

    Industry observers note that in total, Berkshire Hathaway now owns about 106 million Alphabet shares, worth around $30.1 billion. It has been building up this position since 2025, with Abel's predecessor Warren Buffett disclosing in an interview that he, not Abel, "initiated the position.".

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    In a recent development, irrespective of who has been driving these purchases, they have persisted under Abel's watch. During the first half of 2026, Abel added to the original 17.8 million-share position through open-market purchases before making the aforementioned $10 billion investment, part of an $90 billion private placement raised by the Google and YouTube parent.

    Industry observers note that berkshire has participated in private placements before, making large direct investments in several companies during the financial crisis of 2007-2009. Still, this $10 billion deal marked a unique situation: Berkshire investing in a company to fund its growth, not merely to help it shore up its financials.

    It has been revealed that hence, it seems that Berkshire's motivation for this investment largely reflects bullishness about the generative AI growth trend. Also interesting is that it has concentrated this supposed AI wager in Alphabet shares rather than on additional shares of another core Berkshire holding, Apple (AAPL -0.92%). Berkshire last trimmed its Apple position in Q4 2025, but so far in 2026 it has neither increased nor reduced it.

    It has been revealed that although Berkshire ramped up its Alphabet position during Q1 and Q2, it did not add to it during Q3. Is this a sign that investors shouldn't necessarily ride Berkshire's coattails by starting a position today? On one hand, since Berkshire made its initial investment, the shares have surged, rising from less than $200 per share in late 2025 to about $284 as of Nov. 18.

    Industry observers note that on the other hand, back in the summer, Alphabet traded for almost $400 per share, with the recent cooldown in enthusiasm for AI stocks driving a steep pullback. The shares now trade below the roughly $350 per share Berkshire paid for the $10 billion in stock acquired in the private placement. In terms of valuation, the stock also appears reasonably priced at present price levels.

    Sources indicate that currently trading for less than 20 times forward earnings, the shares trade at a discount to other budding AI hyperscalers among Magnificent Seven stocks. Microsoft (MSFT -1.78%), for instance, trades for more than 25 times forward earnings. To be sure, there's a reason investors have started pricing in a discount. The jury's still out on whether massive tech's heavy investment in AI infrastructure, totaling hundreds of billions in capital investment, will translate into worthwhile returns in the long run.

    Alphabet is making between $180 billion and $190 billion on AI-related capital expenditures this year alone, which represents a pretty big wager, even for a trillion-dollar firm. Furthermore, it's unclear whether the dust has settled on this recent AI sell-off. In short, I would base a decision to invest in Alphabet on its fundamentals, not on who's buying or, as it stands today, who's not buying.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 6, Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) peaked at an intraday high of $243.37 per share, reaching a valuation of $5.78 trillion.
    • But it's been a bumpy ride over the last six weeks.
    • While Nvidia's historically inexpensive valuation and its jaw-dropping Data Center segment growth suggest its stock is a bargain, it's also possible that its recent downtrend is just beginning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sean Williams – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    On Oct. 6, Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) peaked at an intraday high of $243.37 per share, reaching a valuation of $5.78 trillion. The face of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out holds a virtual monopoly in enterprise data centers with its several generations of graphics processing units (GPUs).

    But it's been a bumpy ride over the last six weeks. Between its Oct. 6 intraday peak and the Nov. 17 close, Nvidia lost $2.03 trillion in valuation. In just six weeks, Nvidia lost more in market value than all but five S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.02%) companies... one of which is itself.

    While Nvidia's historically inexpensive valuation and its jaw-dropping Data Center segment growth suggest its stock is a bargain, it's also possible that its recent downtrend is just beginning.

    Let's not beat around the bush: the resignation of now-former CEO Jensen Huang following an admission of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and allegations of extramarital relations with up to two employees has left Nvidia without an identity.

    Although Nvidia has an extensive order backlog, superior GPUs, and its pricing power continues to be aided by GPU supply shortages, the firm's innovation schedule (bringing an advanced AI chip to market annually) and its circular financing deals are very much in question.

    BREAKING: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has opened an investigation into Nvidia, $NVDA, amid the Jensen Huang situation, per WSJ. The focus of the investigation includes whether the tech giant’s disclosures misled investors. The Justice Department is also now reportedly leading multiple investigations involving Alice Huang.

    Furthermore, Huang's actions and departure may have breached the trust of clients, consumers, and/or investors. Earlier this week, the Securities and Exchange Commission opened an investigation over whether the manufacturer misled investors in its disclosures.

    Without trust, Nvidia becomes practically uninvestable.

    Although long-term trends strongly suggest that AI will be a game changer and that the benchmark S&P 500 will head higher, historical precedent isn't Nvidia's friend over the short run.

    Every next-substantial-thing technology since (and including) the advent and proliferation of the internet in the mid-1990s has navigated an early-innings bubble. These bubbles form because investors consistently overestimate the pace of adoption and optimization of hyped innovations.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26.

    The good news for AI is that there isn't an adoption issue. Nvidia's quarterly results make it clear that businesses are freely spending to build out their data centers.

    In a recent development, but it's an entirely different story when it comes to optimizing this technology. It took until well after the dot-com bubble burst before businesses figured out how to optimize internet-driven solutions to maximize sales and profits. As with the internet, AI will take time to mature, leaving Nvidia and its peers exposed to a possible bubble-bursting event.

    Lastly, Nvidia's fiscal fourth-quarter gross margin is forecast to dip to 71%-72% from a reported 74.8% (based on generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP) in the fiscal third quarter.

    Although Nvidia's GAAP gross margin has pretty consistently hovered in the low-to-mid 70% range over the trailing three years, the company's fiscal fourth-quarter forecast must have some investors wondering if this is as good as it gets.

    NVDA Gross Profit Margin (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

    Recent findings suggest that this two- to three-percentage-point dip in GAAP gross margin reflects higher memory prices and the near-term ramp-up associated with Vera Rubin shipments. But if GPU supply picks up from its competition, as is expected, Nvidia's pricing power and GAAP gross margin would be expected to wane over time.

    In other words, Nvidia may not be the slam-dunk bargain it appears to be.

    #3626. Fantasy Football: From chasing history to breakouts, 1 thing to watch in all 32 WR rooms for the second half

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3398 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Fantasy Football: From chasing history to breakouts, 1 thing to watch in all 32 WR rooms for the second half

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With the second half of the season in full swing, here's what Yahoo analyst Matt Harmon is looking for in each team's WR room for fantasy football.
    • Industry observers note that after a blistering start to the year, Flowers is now WR8 in yards per route run and WR16 in points per game.
    • When DJ Moore has been available for the Bills, all the mainstay passing-game players get a bump.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With the second half of the season in full swing, here's what Yahoo analyst Matt Harmon is looking for in each team's WR room for fantasy football.

    Industry observers note that after a blistering start to the year, Flowers is now WR8 in yards per route run and WR16 in points per game. It was tracking to be so much better than this before quarterback chaos sunk the Ravens' passing game. In Jacoby Brissett's first start, the Ravens dropped back over 50 times, a rarity in the Lamar Jackson era, but the passing tree wasn't consolidated whatsoever. Flowers was targeted on 14.9% of his routes, the lowest rate of the season. Both fantasy managers and a Ravens team that desperately needs to win require the ball in Flowers' hands much more often than that, even if he ultimately fumbled the game away in Week 10.

    When DJ Moore has been available for the Bills, all the mainstay passing-game players get a bump. On plays where Moore is on the field, Khalil Shakir averages 2.03 yards per route and Dalton Kincaid averages 3.15. Kincaid specifically drops to 1.97 when Moore isn't on the field. This is because Moore, who averages a whopping 16.6 air yards per target, has been a huge add as a coverage-dictator and vertical threat. Moore isn't going to be a WR1-level producer but he's key to the health of this offense and is capable of spike weeks in this ecosystem.

    Right now, the Bengals have the WR4 and WR6 in points per game on their roster. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been masterful this season with Joe Burrow playing the best football of his career. Each receiver has five games inside the top-10 of weekly fantasy scoring. The Bengals offense has used condensed formations, and the leap in their offensive line's pass-blocking has been a key factor. Quietly, Dohnte Meyers is emerging as a credible option as the WR3 who can play multiple positions, which has also allowed them to be more creative with the deployment. I see no reason this train slows down any time soon.

    In a recent development, so far this season, Denzel Boston has been used as a downfield X-receiver and KC Concepcion has been a movement option who runs over 60% of his routes from the slot. I'm not critiquing that deployment, as both are excellent options in those roles and have been fantastic to start their rookie seasons. However, I believe Boston is capable of being weaponized with some reps as a major slot and Concepcion can win outside against man coverage. If those roles start to blend down the stretch, or especially in future seasons, these guys can be even more productive.

    Sources indicate that call it hope or call it cope, but we can blame my favorite strength-of-schedule zealot, Justin Boone, for even getting me to keep the light on. Coming out of the bye, the Broncos have games against the Raiders (twice), Steelers, Jets, Dolphins, Bills and Patriots. Only the Steelers look like a potential trouble spot for passing games. I hesitate to say it can't get worse but it would be tough to imagine. Waddle has finished inside the top-24 weekly scoring receivers just twice, which is only one fewer game than every other Denver wide receiver combined (Pat Bryant twice, Courtland Sutton once). I'm hoping the offense has a clearer vision for how to maximize the player they traded major draft picks for, as well as a more confident player under center.

    Recent findings suggest that in his last two games coming back from the team's Week 8 bye, Tank Dell has run a route on 55% and 54.8% of the dropbacks. The team has used guys like Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him and had him in a rotation with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kayshon Boutte. There's a good chance this usage holds for Dell as he continues to work his way back from a serious injury. I'm still comfortable betting on him as an upside WR3 because he looks great on tape and is being used on downfield breaking routes. You just have to know you're dealing with a volatile projection with that playing time.

    In a recent development, the Colts traded their best 2026 receiver at the deadline in Josh Downs and sent away a steady veteran in Keenan Allen. Their highly paid X-receiver, Alec Pierce, is on IR and I'm not expecting him to be back this year. Laquon Treadwell will lead this group in routes run as the every-down X-receiver going forward in a passing game that's been among the worst in the NFL, thanks to quarterback play. We don't need to fret the Colts' room much at this stage but I'm at least curious if any young players can flash to earn a role in 2027. Deion Burks is an interesting rookie with some juice who has gotten reps all year as a downfield Z-receiver.

    In a recent development, the Jaguars are one of the toughest teams to prepare for in the NFL right now. This offense can run so many concepts out of multiple personnel groupings and has a litany of viable role players. Meanwhile, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington are two of the league's most productive receivers on throws of 10-20 air yards. In competitive games and good matchups, these two should roll, especially Washington.

    Industry observers note that josh Downs' arrival in Kansas City paid immediate dividends for the offense. He was targeted five times on eight routes. Those numbers are only going up. The question is how high he can go and who comes off the field more often. Xavier Worthy seems like the natural answer given his play through three seasons, but his speed also brings tactical value by lifting coverages. Rashee Rice and Downs should be more complementary as they go. Additionally, Cyrus Allen's emergence as a talented route-runner and deep-ball option makes this even more complicated. I think Downs emerges as an every-week fantasy starter but we have playing time questions to answer to understand the ceiling.

    According to recent reports, tre Tucker has been the team's best receiver but will be a free agent. He's a good player but mostly a vertical-only receiver. Meanwhile, Jalen Nailor has looked overstretched as an every-down starter. Second-year receiver Jack Bech is a nice role player but hasn't emerged as a highly-targeted option and missed a chunk of time with an injury. The Raiders will use the rest of the season to simply assess if any of these guys will be in the rotation in 2027, or if they will need to start fresh.

    I've been ready to see more of Tre' Harris and less of Quentin Johnston since the first month of the season. Johnston has never fully developed and, frankly, looks like he's regressed in 2026. Meanwhile, Harris continues to flash a nice ability to separate and play multiple positions. He's run a route on more than 90% of the dropbacks just twice this year and compiled 60 yards on three catches in Week 4 and 86 on five last week. I'd love to watch Ladd McConkey take off in the back half, but I just worry he's not physically up for the task. He averages 2.25 yards per route run this year, so he's been good, but he just can't stay on the field.

    Caleb Douglas leads all rookies with 2.27 yards per route run and the tape has been rock-solid. He is clearly a hit for the Dolphins. Now, let's find out how good he is. Malik Willis' injury will likely complicate things from a production standpoint. Yet, Douglas registered a season-high 155 air yards and caught three passes for 71 yards last week with Kyle McCord under center. Douglas has hit at least 70 yards in three of his last four games.

    When the Patriots return from their bye week, they will do so without Drake Maye under center. The season is slowly slipping away for this team as they are buried under a mountain of injuries. It's just not going to be their year. The rest of the season should be dedicated to figuring out which members of the wide receiver room should have major roles in 2027 and beyond. That includes A.J. Brown, who has been unable to stay healthy and doesn't look right when he's been available. I'm not sure he'll be on the roster next year, which leaves Romeo Doubs and a collection of WR3 and WR4 types. This room needs an upgrade.

    Despite playing in very different roles, we haven't seen many games where AD Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. both go off at the same time. That's especially tough when Garrett Wilson is available. The Jets have a strong trio of receivers with these guys on the roster and my sense is that they'll all be on the team in 2027. The rest of the way, we need to look at their individual matchups and success to try and pinpoint the right weeks Mitchell and Cooper can get going. This will also help us assess what the pecking order looks like behind Wilson next season in what, hopefully, is an improved overall ecosystem.

    Recent findings suggest that germie Bernard looked like he might be one of those second-half-of-the-season rookie breakouts about a month ago. Yet, he's failed to clear 30 yards in any of his last three games. While I think he's a good player, you wonder if he has missed his window to cement a starting job. The Steelers will likely get veteran Michael Pittman Jr. back soon, along with Roman Wilson. The Bernard and Wilson playing time splits will be quite interesting since Wilson gave this team a real man coverage answer early in the year.

    The Titans have found an answer to boosting Cam Ward in recent weeks: Tennessee has used no huddle on 45% of their snaps in each game on either side of the bye week. No other team is even above 18%. Ward operates well with tempo and from spread concepts. No surprise, this has resulted in Ward's two best games of the season. That's without Carnell Tate in the mix, who has been excellent on tape this year and a real weapon down the field. Once he's healthy, Tate's ability to rapidly separate on routes over the middle in this newly introduced-look attack should result in some big weeks.

    It has been revealed that I'll be frank, this might be the bleakest wide receiver room I can remember in recent memory after they lost Michael Wilson for the season and placed Kendrick Bourne on IR. The only guy who is moderately interesting is Day 3 rookie, Reggie Virgil. He's a slower, poor man's Robbie Anderson from his days with the Panthers. Someone has to run routes for this team; catches may be optional.

    It has been revealed that we know what Drake London can do but not enough people are giving Jahan Dotson praise for the rebound season he is having. Dotson leads all wide receivers with 30-plus targets with 21.9 yards per catch. He's been a real nice answer for the team as a deep option down the field. His ability here has allowed the Falcons to keep London in a movement Z and slot-heavy role.

    According to recent reports, the Panthers need to change up their approach on offense. What worked to smash teams early in the season has become unworkable as pass-protection issues have cropped up. Bryce Young leads the NFL in pass attempts with pressure arriving in 2.5 seconds or faster. On those throws, Tetairoa McMillan averages almost 17 air yards per target and Jalen Coker is at almost 10. These receivers run long, developing routes to hit chunk plays and that's a thin line to walk when you can't hold up in protection.

    This season, Rome Odunze averages 14.9 air yards per target, which leads the team by a wide margin and Luther Burden is at 7.4. The Bears aren't doing anything wrong here and both are thriving in their respective roles; there's just no overlap between the two. I believe Odunze can win in the short area as a chain-mover more often and Burden can get open in the intermediate area. Blending those would allow Odunze to be targeted more often and keep Burden involved for all four quarters.

    Sources indicate that at this rate, I'd be shocked if George Pickens returns to Dallas after an up-and-down season with the team on the franchise tag, especially with CeeDee Lamb turning in a dominant performance. Pickens will likely be motivated to put up more big performances after his Week 10 outing, which was the second-highest scoring game for a receiver all season. Keep an eye on his likely replacement, Ryan Flournoy, who has scored as a top-24 receiver in five of his last six games. He's already a viable option.

    According to recent reports, over the last five weeks, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams account for 51% of the team's targets. Sam LaPorta is a relatively distant third at 14%. For much of the last two years, it's really been a push and pull between LaPorta and Williams for the second target option — rarely have they popped off together. The Lions have jumped their use of heavy personnel considerably in this post-bye span, which has contributed to the wideouts getting more burn, especially Williams, who runs a route on a team-high 90% of the dropbacks since Week 6. This is how we get more consistent weekly production from the volatile wideout.

    Sources indicate that matthew Golden has been one of the breakout stars at the wide receiver position this year. He's the WR8 in points per game behind his teammate Christian Watson. That's been despite leading the league in drops by a considerable margin. Fantasy Points Data has charged Golden with 13 drops this year, almost double the amount of the second-highest receiver in AD Mitchell with eight. He's also won just three of his 11 contested targets. I'm always the first guy to suggest you just live with drop challenges and continue to build the wideout's confidence so they can push past them. The Packers and Jordan Love appear to be taking that approach. If he can ever clean these issues up, the ceiling is quite high for Golden and he's already been excellent; scary proposition.

    The Rams used a ton of 20 personnel in Week 10, with both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams on the field along with three wide receivers. For the most part, that was a collection of small speed-based options to hit major plays while the backs operate as checkdown outlets. It was a good bit of problem-solving by Sean McVay as injuries hit the receiver room but it's likely not sustainable. Now, if we can add Davante Adams to the mix as an intermediate answer to balance the scales, it could become a feature personnel grouping. The veteran could return in Week 12 or 13.

    It has been revealed that I'm not asking for much here. Justin Jefferson should continue to be the featured player. He registered 13 targets in Week 10. He had not seen 13-plus looks in a game since the Sam Darnold 2024 season. We just need complementary pieces to add pop to the other touches and layer in new dimensions to the offense with Kirk Cousins under center. I'll admit to enjoying the work of Myles Price and Tai Felton in place of some of the other guys who were previously putting the Vikings into schematic binds. Both averaged 6.0 yards or more after the catch per reception. Cousins having someone to spit the ball out to in the short area and get additional yards helps keep the offense on schedule.

    Industry observers note that since Jordyn Tyson has been activated, he's taken over half his snaps from the slot and lined up off the ball on 80% of them. No wide receiver has been used in motion more than Tyson the last two weeks. He's been able to gobble up easy receptions while being targeted on 38% of his routes. That's awesome for his usage in fantasy but it was not a great initiative for the Saints' offense, particularly in Week 10, when they ranked 23rd out of 28 teams in my offensive efficiency score. Tyson can get open in the intermediate area and Chris Olave shouldn't be left to run vertical stretch routes only. Tyson is an awesome player in this slot movement role but we can't overindex on the short passes, especially since he's not a run-after-catch threat.

    It has been revealed that malik Nabers was looking close to 100% healthy prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye and enjoyed some strong moments with J.J. McCarthy against the Texans. The two games since have been less enjoyable. While it's easy to blame McCarthy for the problems and he's far from blameless, Nabers has left some plays on the field as well. I hold Nabers in extremely high regard and believe he is the next guy who could graduate to Tier 1 (Ja'Marr Chase, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, etc. grouping) at the receiver position. I'd love to see him knock down that door in the back-half of the season. He needs to rebound from two of his less inspiring outings in back-to-back weeks.

    In Weeks 7 to 9, Makai Lemon owned a near 27% share of the Eagles targets. Despite four out-of-character drops, Lemon still averaged 61.7 yards per game and snagged 19 receptions. He was starting to look like the layup slot funnel you'd hope for from his archetype of receiver. However, the target competition is about to ramp up with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due back from injuries soon. How the Lemon and Smith, in particular, target distribution goes will inform us on how the situation may play out next season, as the Eagles play out the string for the rest of 2026.

    The 49ers have the oldest wide receiver room I can remember with five guys over 31 years old taking snaps for the team in 2026. Yet, they keep rolling. Deebo Samuel Sr. has settled into a pure gadget role and barely operates as a true receiver. Keenan Allen arrived in the middle of last week and immediately earned a first down on 19.1% of his routes. He's going to be quite helpful down the stretch. When Mike Evans is healthy, he's still a fantastic starting X-receiver.

    Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 1,207 yards on 79 catches (109 targets) through 10 weeks of the NFL season. You'd do backflips if your favorite sleeper receiver did that over a full season. Smith-Njigba is on pace to clear 2,000 yards this season. He'd be the first wideout in NFL history to do it. Based on his own individual play despite teams crafting coverages to stop him, and the lack of a true secondary threat, there's no reason to expect him to slow down anytime soon.

    According to recent reports, I'm very confident that Emeka Egbuka is a good NFL player but the Buccaneers need him to be great. We've yet to see that version of the player this season. To be fair, Egbuka has been dogged by injuries since training camp and the guy we saw against the Bears prior to the bye week was the worst version I've watched on tape in 2026. Hopefully a week off helps him get back to form as he heads into a good matchup against the Lions defense. Egbuka's 20.8% slot rate in Week 9 was the lowest of the season; that needs to rise in future weeks.

    It has been revealed that since the team returned from the bye, Antonio Williams has led the team in routes run. He looks good on tape and gets easy separation in the intermediate area. However, he hasn't been consistently involved in the offense (16% target share). The Commanders spread the ball around, and he's competing with an excellent receiver in Stefon Diggs, who leads the team over the last three weeks with a 25% target-per-route rate. Williams can still make some big plays but we need him to get the ball more consistently to be an every-week option in fantasy. He does remain and excellent buy in dynasty leagues.

    Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

    📅 04 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud firm CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    It has been revealed that chatterjee mentioned CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    Industry observers note that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Sources indicate that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell stated. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    According to recent reports, powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    It has been revealed that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Recent findings suggest that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the tech giant if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he noted. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    In a recent development, "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," noted Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    Sources indicate that devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    #3604. Latest Update: Gold's bad year is getting worse. Why its price keeps falling

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1458 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Gold's bad year is getting worse. Why its price keeps falling

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1458 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Precious metals investors can be forgiven if they feel like the past year has given them whiplash.
    • According to recent reports, following a torrid run, which saw the price of gold hit newly introduced records 53 times in 2025, gold hit a historic high of $5,589.38 an ounce on Jan.
    • A convergence of factors pushed gold to historic highs earlier this year, according to Suki Cooper, global head of commodities research at Standard Chartered, the London-based multinational bank.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Precious metals investors can be forgiven if they feel like the past year has given them whiplash.

    According to recent reports, following a torrid run, which saw the price of gold hit newly introduced records 53 times in 2025, gold hit a historic high of $5,589.38 an ounce on Jan. 28, only to take an almost equally historic nosedive. On Wednesday, gold fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025, roughly a third below its peak.

    A convergence of factors pushed gold to historic highs earlier this year, according to Suki Cooper, global head of commodities research at Standard Chartered, the London-based multinational bank. Now a different convergence is bringing the price down.

    "Gold can behave as a commodity or a currency," Cooper remarked.

    Which role it plays depends on the factors dominating the market and the psyche of investors, and right now, it's the currency argument that is bringing the precious metal down.

    Cooper said gold's climb began with strong physical demand that started in 2022 and raised the floor under prices. A second phase followed as investors rethought gold's place in their portfolios. With the cost of holding a non-yielding asset falling, they started thinking about the metal for the longer term. That, Cooper said, marked a turnaround.

    Until early 2025, Cooper noted, long-term investors, especially those in gold-backed exchange-traded funds, had been cutting their exposure, which effectively added supply to the market. Last year, that reversed: ETF holdings, led by the SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), rose by roughly 800 tons and helped absorb the market's excess supply.

    "There was a lot of one-way interest, a lot of appetite to buy but not to sell," Cooper mentioned.

    With selling in the secondary market staying muted, prices kept rising. By the end of 2025, net ETF holdings had passed 4,000 tons. Globally, gold ETFs had their strongest year ever for inflows, $89 billion, led by North America, according to the World Gold Council, with assets more than doubling to $559 billion in total.

    A weaker dollar, lower bond yields and worries about global debt "set the foundation for gold to hit highs in 2026," Cooper remarked.

    Investors who had been under-exposed to the metal kept buying.

    Evan Mills, a financial advisor with Scholar Financial Advising, a fee-only firm in Winston-Salem, N.C., said the lower interest rates, expectations of further rate cuts and a weakening dollar, were all reasons for investors to favor gold.

    It has been revealed that "It was a perfect spot to be in if you were an investor in gold and commodities as a whole," Mills noted. And investors did extremely well, especially with lower interest rates. "Cash doesn't do well in that environment, so a lot of people looked toward other places to hold their cash and maintain purchasing power," Mills said.

    The speed of the rally made some investors uneasy, and there was growing talk that the Fed could tighten. Then, Cooper noted, the Middle East conflict broke out and gold changed roles. It stopped acting as a portfolio safe haven and became "a liquidity provider.".

    Recent findings suggest that cooper explained that because it was liquid and easy to sell, investors sold it to raise cash, which set off the first correction. Since then, she remarked, markets have been pricing in what the Fed will do.

    "In 2026, the Fed has leaned more toward higher interest rates," Mills remarked.

    This week, the Federal Reserve Board of Governors member Christopher Waller mentioned a 50-basis point rate hike may be necessary to "shock people.".

    "There are higher Treasury yields and a strengthening dollar, so the opportunity cost of holding an asset that doesn't produce income is much higher," Mills mentioned.

    Mills remarked that in the current situation, gold investors are missing out on an environment in which cash actually does well, with money market funds that can pay 4% to 5%.

    "Cash maintains purchasing power, and you don't need to put it in an illiquid asset or one where you're relying on another person to see the value," Mills noted.

    From 2025 to 2026, gold didn't become any less scarce; the alternatives to owning it became more attractive.

    "Stocks, bonds, the classic portfolio mix, all became a lot more attractive, so people looked at the opportunity cost and decided it wasn't worth holding gold anymore," Mills said.

    This has been the case for other metals in 2026 as well, with silver plummeting from an all-time high price.

    In a recent development, after an extraordinary rally, it's easy to start questioning gold. Mills remarked investors should start by remembering that expectations were extremely high. "When expectations are 20% or 30% returns in a year, then of course when returns drop, people start to panic," Mills said.

    Panic shouldn't be the watchword for gold investors, but caution should remain.

    "In the short term, with real yields going up and the dollar likely strengthening with future Fed hikes, I'd be cautious about gold in the overall portfolio," Mills said.

    For investors, the key is to understand why gold is in your portfolio to begin with.

    Industry observers note that "If you're looking for it to be a short-term purchase, then gold likely doesn't belong in your portfolio at all," Mills said. If the metal is seen as a hedge, gold can remain a valuable part of a portfolio, but it can still be a poor investment depending on the price you pay to get in.

    "If you're looking at gold to be the growth section of your portfolio, you're likely going to be disappointed," he mentioned. "Gold is insurance, not an engine, and the mistake is buying insurance when its price has skyrocketed," he added.

    Recent findings suggest that for investors who bought at January's peak as a modest, long-term hedge, a sharp downturn doesn't defeat the purpose, he said. "You have nothing to really worry about, because that's what the whole goal of gold was.".

    Gold tends to do well when the dollar weakens or when markets and geopolitics turn uncertain, Mills mentioned, and when those pressures fade, the rest of a portfolio should pick up the slack.

    "That's the whole point of insurance, and the whole point of diversification," he mentioned. "Gold does well when the other parts of your portfolio might be slacking, and when they flip-flop, that's a good thing.".

    According to recent reports, other commodities experts say gold remains a good long-term bet. Amy Gower, head of metals and mining strategy at Morgan Stanley, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" that there are "still lots of reasons" for investors to hang on to their gold despite the correction this year.

    Philip Diehl, former director of the U.S. Mint and now president of U.S. Money Reserve, an Austin, Texas-based distributor of government-issued gold, silver and platinum coins, mentioned the long-term case for gold is still in place, but the combination of abrupt shifts in U.S. trade policy and geopolitical alliances, along with the Iran war, qualifies as a black swan event for the precious metal.

    Sources indicate that "The fundamentals that drove that bull market remain in place. They were interrupted by the Cat 5 hurricane that was unleashed in the Persian Gulf in an unwise war," Diehl stated.

    He expects that to change after American voters "issued a mandate" to end that war two weeks ago.

    "I'm confident gold prices will return to their upward trajectory in 2027 as oil prices normalize and prices fall at the pump, allowing interest rates to stabilize," Diehl said.

    Central banks continue to buy gold, with the highest monthly total in September, according to the World Gold Council, though overall purchasing is 7% lower than the same period last year.

    Marc Chandler, managing partner and chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets, mentioned surveys suggest that, in aggregate, that will not change. "However, don't only think about China or U.S. rivals," Chandler said, noting that the World Gold Council has identified Poland, a NATO member, as one of the larger buyers for most of this year.

    "Retail has been burned," Chandler noted. "Higher interest rates have made non-interest-bearing assets less attractive, including bitcoin.".

    Chandler remarked that the price of gold is headed to $3,500 to $3,600. Gold hit a fresh low below $3,700 on Thursday morning.

    "There is nothing on the charts that claims a low is in place," Chandler mentioned. "For the anxious bottom pickers, I urge caution and being patient to see some reversal pattern. For the most part, the decline looks fairly orderly.".

    "Gold is still very expensive compared to anything but the last two years," Chandler noted, noting that gold's 10-year (120-month) moving average is about $2,127 and its 20-year (240-month) moving average is about $1,666.
